Solution
Words: 140
iv OurBigBook.com
The literal expression in the original PDF is undefined. Indeed, hyperbolic tangent satisfies tanhw=sinhw/coshw, and
cosh(inπ/4)=cos(nπ/4)=0when n≡2(mod4).
(21)
Already the n=2 summand contains tanh(iπ/2), a pole. The shifted term has the same issue when n≡3(mod4). Thus this is not a finite sum of defined complex numbers, and it has no literal real or imaginary part. Cancelling two undefined terms is not ordinary arithmetic.
There is nevertheless a natural interpretation by meromorphic telescoping cancellation. Insert the same small positive real shift ε into every hyperbolic tangent argument. Each term is then finite, and the telescoping sum is
S(ε)=tanh(ε+121iπ/4)−tanhε.
(22)
Since hyperbolic tangent has period iπ, its first argument can be reduced to ε+iπ/4. Taking the limit gives
ε→0+lim​S(ε)=i,ℜ=0,ℑ=1.​
(23)
This is a common-shift continuation of the sum, plausibly the intended telescoping answer. It requires that additional convention; it is not the value of the expression as printed.

The finite form of Taylor's theorem with the first n terms is
f(x)=k=0∑n−1​k!f(k)(a)​(x−a)k+Rn​(x),Rn​(x)=n!f(n)(ξ)​(x−a)n,​
(54)
where ξ lies strictly between a and x for x=a. A sufficient hypothesis is that f has continuous derivatives through order n−1 on the interval joining the endpoints and an nth derivative in its interior. The displayed polynomial has degree at most n−1; its Taylor remainder uses the nth derivative, not the (n+1)st. At x=a the remainder is zero. This is a finite Taylor polynomial identity and does not require an infinite Taylor series to converge.

Random sampling without replacement assigns each of the ten distinguishable pieces to each lunch with the same probability. Five pieces of each type therefore give
P(A1​)=21​,P(B2​)=21​.​
(61)
One can check the second probability by conditioning on the first lunch:
P(B2​)=P(B2​∣A1​)P(A1​)+P(B2​∣B1​)P(B1​)=95​21​+94​21​=21​.
(62)
The identical marginal probabilities do not imply independence of the draws.

Condition on an apple occupying position two in a uniformly random ordering. The nine other positions then contain four apples and five bananas, each equally likely to occupy position three. The conditional probability is therefore
P(A3​∣A2​)=94​.​
(63)
This uses exchangeability of the unconditioned positions; there is no need to assume the first lunch contained a particular fruit.

Each position has apple probability 1/2. Applying Bayes' theorem to the preceding conditional probability gives
P(A2​∣A3​)=P(A3​)P(A3​∣A2​)P(A2​)​=1/2(4/9)(1/2)​=94​.​
(64)
This also agrees with exchangeability of the second and third positions.

By the inclusion-exclusion principle for probabilities,
P(B1​∪A2​)=P(B1​)+P(A2​)−P(B1​∩A2​).
(65)
After an initial banana, five of the nine remaining pieces are apples, so the intersection probability is (1/2)(5/9)=5/18. Consequently
P(B1​∪A2​)=21​+21​−185​=1813​.​
(66)
As a check, the complementary event is an apple followed by a banana, which also has probability 5/18.

Let Ij​ be the indicator random variable of an apple in lunch j. The number remaining is R=5−I1​−I2​−I3​. Each expected value E[Ij​]=P(Aj​)=1/2. The linearity of expectation therefore gives
E[R]=5−3(21​)=27​ apples.​
(67)
Although the indicator random variables are dependent under sampling without replacement, the linearity of expectation needs no independence assumption.

Let N count rotten pieces. Each item supplies an independent Bernoulli trial with success probability p, so N has a binomial distribution with parameters 10,p. There are (n10​) choices of the rotten items, and each such choice has probability pn(1−p)10−n. Hence
P(N=n)=(n10​)pn(1−p)10−n,n=0,…,10.​
(68)
For p=0 or p=1, interpret this as the corresponding distribution concentrated at zero or ten; no ambiguous 00 evaluation is needed.

Write N=∑j=110​Xj​, where the independent Bernoulli random variables indicate rottenness. Since Xj2​=Xj​, their variances are E[Xj2​]−E[Xj​]2=p−p2. The independence makes all cross covariances zero, so
Var(N)=10p(1−p),σN​=10p(1−p)​ pieces.​
(69)
This standard deviation vanishes at p=0 and p=1, when the count is certain.

A three-dimensional rotation matrix is an orthogonal matrix with determinant +1. Here detA=b(a2−d2). For the branch d=0, the determinant condition gives b=1; for the branch a=0, it gives b=−1. Hence
(a,b,c)T∈{(1,1,1)T,(−1,1,1)T,(0,−1,0)T,(0,−1,2)T}.​

The first is the identity rotation; the remaining three are half-turns. Their fixed axes are respectively the y axis, the direction (1,0,−1) and the direction (1,0,1). The identity is included under the usual rotation matrix convention.

Equivalently ∇ψ=(x,y,z) and its divergence is three.

The sloping height relation on the cone is z=b(1−r/a). A parametric equation of its curved surface is therefore
R(r,θ)=(rcosθ,rsinθ,b(1−r/a)),0≤r≤a,0≤θ<2π.
(86)
Its two tangent vectors are Rr​=(cosθ,sinθ,−b/a) and Rθ​=r(−sinθ,cosθ,0). Multiplication by dr and dθ produces the two infinitesimal sides requested in the paper. Their cross product is the vector area element:
dS=(Rr​×Rθ​)drdθ=r(ab​cosθ,ab​sinθ,1)drdθ.​
(87)
Its radial component is positive, so this normal vector points outwards from the solid cone. Taking its norm gives the scalar area element
dS=r1+a2b2​​drdθ.​
(88)
The parametric equation degenerates at the apex, but that single point contributes no area.

∫C​F⋅dS=∫02π​∫0a​brdrdθ=πa2b.​

F(x(t))=(2t,1,1),G(x(t))=(2t2,1−2t+2t2,1−2t+2t2).

Taking each dot product with dx evaluates the line integrals:

The proposed parametric equation traces precisely the same oriented segment, with a different speed. Set u=tn, which increases from zero to one, and du=ntn−1dt. Direct substitution gives the line integrals
∫F⋅dx∫G⋅dx​=∫01​(2−2tn)ntn−1dt=∫01​(2−2u)du=1,=∫01​(2−4tn+2t2n)ntn−1dt=∫01​(2−4u+2u2)du=32​.​
(96)
Thus both values are unchanged. The derivative of u vanishes at the initial endpoint for n>1, but the monotone integration by substitution is still valid. This is invariance under reparametrization of one curve, which applies even to a nonconservative vector field; it is not evidence of general path independence.

∫G⋅dx=0+0+∫01​1dz=1=32​.​
